content.user_title: Build a compliant email reactivation program
content.value_statement: Inactive subscribers can harm deliverability and leave consent status unclear. This skill creates a staged recovery plan with re-consent and a clear suppression outcome.
actual_capabilities: Defines a lapsed cohort using stated engagement windows.
Designs a staged offer ladder with timing and exit conditions.
Adds a re-consent action for recovered subscribers.
Specifies a terminal suppression rule for non-responders.
Labels unavailable metrics as estimated rather than measured.
Produces handoff facts for consent and lifecycle owners.
limitations: Does not send emails or connect to an email platform by itself.
Does not create or verify legal consent records.
Does not calculate deliverability scores or enforce quality gates.
Requires user-provided engagement and suppression policy details.

use_cases.title: Clean an inactive newsletter segment
use_cases.description: Create a re-permission sequence and sunset rule for subscribers with no recent engagement.

use_cases.title: Recover dormant customers
use_cases.description: Plan an offer ladder for inactive customers while setting a clear return path to active nurture.

use_cases.title: Prepare a consent-safe reactivation review
use_cases.description: Document re-consent actions and suppression outcomes for a marketing operations review.

prompt_templates.title: Define a basic win-back campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a win-back campaign for subscribers with no opens in 90 days. We use a newsletter and have no discount available.

prompt_templates.title: Add a staged incentive
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a three-step reactivation ladder for inactive customers. We can offer free shipping after the first reminder.

prompt_templates.title: Create a re-permission plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a re-permission sweep for subscribers with no click in 180 days. Include the confirmation action and suppression rule.

prompt_templates.title: Plan from operational inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this engagement summary and suppression policy, define the cohort, offer ladder, re-consent action, terminal states, assumptions, and handoffs.

output_examples.input: Re-engage newsletter subscribers with no opens in 90 days. No incentive is available.
output: Cohort: subscribers with no opens for 90 days, excluding suppressed and hard-bounced addresses.
Step 1: ask subscribers to confirm continued interest within seven days.
Terminal rule: suppress non-responders after the defined final window.

output_examples.input: Recover dormant customers with a free-shipping incentive.
output: Start with a value reminder, then offer free shipping only to non-responders.
Require a click-to-confirm action before returning a subscriber to active nurture.
Record consent and suppression outcomes in the designated consent system.

best_practices: Use verified suppression and consent records before creating a cohort.
Set a finite number of touches and a clear end date.
Label assumptions and missing metrics clearly for review.
anti_patterns: Do not repeatedly contact subscribers after the terminal suppression window.
Do not treat an email open as fresh consent.
Do not include already suppressed or hard-bounced addresses.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails?
faq.answer: No. It creates a program specification for your email platform or team.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide an inactivity window, available incentive, platform context, and suppression policy.

faq.question: Can it use missing engagement data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft a plan and label cohort metrics as estimated.

faq.question: Does re-engagement equal consent?
faq.answer: No. The plan requires an explicit re-consent action for recovered subscribers.

faq.question: How many messages should the ladder include?
faq.answer: Use a limited ladder, typically three or four touches, with a defined stop rule.

faq.question: What happens to non-responders?
faq.answer: The plan assigns them to a confirmed sunset state for suppression after the final window.
